title: A Digital Model to Explain the Necessity of Prostaglandin E1 After Balloon Atrial Septostomy in D-Transposition of the Great Arteries
content:
Objective: Patients with D-Transposition of the Great Arteries (TGA) often require prostaglandin E1 (PGE) even after balloon atrial septostomy (BAS). This study builds a computer simulation that analyzes whether or not elevated pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) could explain the profound hypoxemia seen in some patients after PGE discontinuation.
Methods: We developed a systems-based mathematical model of TGA incorporating systemic and pulmonary circulations, atrial septal defect (ASD), and patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) with bidirectional atrial mixing. The effects of BAS and PGE withdrawal were modeled by altering atrial and ductal resistances, respectively. Using Monte Carlo sampling, 500 virtual patients with variable pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) and systemic vascular resistance (SVR) were simulated. Key outcomes included relative changes in systemic oxygen saturation (ΔSsa), systemic flow (ΔQs/Qs), effective pulmonary flow (ΔQp,eff/Qp,eff), and oxygen delivery (ΔDO₂/DO₂).
Results: Regression analysis demonstrated that each unit increase in PVR was associated with a 0.4% decrease in ΔSsa, an 8.8% reduction in ΔQs/Qs, an 8.8% reduction in ΔQp,eff/Qp,eff, and a 9.5% reduction in ΔDO₂/DO₂ (all p<  0.01). In contrast, SVR had smaller but favorable effects, with each unit increase associated with a 0.3% improvement in ΔSsa, 0.6% increase in ΔQs/Qs, 1.6% increase in ΔQp,eff/Qp,eff, and 1.0% increase in ΔDO₂/DO₂. Importantly, discontinuation of PGE and ductal closure often resulted in lower systemic oxygen saturation but higher systemic oxygen delivery due to increased systemic blood flow, an effect most pronounced in patients with low PVR.
Conclusions: The effectiveness of BAS in eliminating ductal dependence is strongly influenced by vascular tone. Elevated PVR markedly limits the benefit of atrial decompression, while higher SVR exerts modestly protective effects. These findings explain clinical variability in BAS outcomes and highlight that systemic oxygen delivery—not saturation alone—should guide assessment of post-BAS physiology in neonates with TGA.
